name: Spruce green
lede: Spruce Green is a dark, moderately saturated green from the 1927 RAL paint standard, and its screen value is an exact match for another RAL name, Pearl Green.

sections.title: Two RAL names, one screen value
sections.body: ColorHub's library traces Spruce Green to RAL 6035, a 1927 German paint standard, with no record in Ridgway, ISCC-NBS or Maerz and Paul [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[cossack]] and [[spruce]], at The nearest distinct named color on file is [[hunter-green]], about 4.8 units of CIEDE2000 away [1]. Our own tagging files it under the Greens, alongside [[green]] and [[forest-green]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Spruce Green in only 26 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed [2]. It plays a shadow more often than a highlight, 54 percent of the time, consistent with how dark it is [2]. The earliest dated match is Lucas Cranach the Elder's 1522 *Portrait of a Woman*, four centuries before RAL's standard, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that the name or paint existed that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
